Gudde, N., Larivé, J.-F. and Yugo, M. (2019). CO2 reduction technologies. Opportunities within the EU refining system (2030/2050). Qualitative & Quantitative assessment for the production of conventional fossil fuels (Scope 1 & 2). Concawe Report no. 8/19, Brussels, July 2019. Prepared for the Concawe Special Task Force Refinery 2050 (STF-2).

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 14; Summary pages are roman numerals, cited as Summary). A system-level study of the EU-28 refining sector (80 refineries), so most numbers are sector totals or assumptions rather than plant data. Main file (25 technology-contexts): the unit-cost and performance assumptions the study uses (electrolysers Table 4.4.5.2-1; SMR capex; CO2 capture parameters Table 4.5.2-1 and cost ranges; electric boiler, electric and fired process heater, heat pump, CHP and ORC capex and efficiencies; oxy-fuel FCC retrofit; and 2050 Median abatement costs). Whole-system results (process efficiency saving % and capex, Table 6.1-1; all abatement costs of Table 6.5-1 with column positions read from page coordinates) are in the measures file. Prices: euro and dollar price years are never stated; publication year 2019 used and flagged. Several costs are quoted from SINTEF (2017), DNV (2018), DEA (2016) or Towler (2013) (reprinted). No SEC per t of refinery product is printed; US DoE bandwidth energy intensities (Table A.1.1-1) are printed with an apparent units error (MMBTU/bbl should be thousand Btu/bbl) and were left in other-values. Figures (capex, abatement curves, efficiency projections) are charts without printed values and were not read. Report 9/19A (separate extraction) covers the Refinery 2050 appendices.
